source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Offer resilience training while leaving staffing levels, workload, schedules, and administrative processes unchanged.","B":"Focus on individual coping and avoid reviewing work-system causes because organizational changes may be disruptive.","C":"Review operations with staff and address modifiable drivers such as staffing, workload, scheduling, administrative burden, safety, and support.","D":"Increase mandatory overtime to fill staffing gaps while expanding mindfulness and other individual wellness resources."}}
source_row.rationale: NIOSH's Impact Wellbeing approach explicitly moves beyond placing the burden on individual resilience. Hospital leaders should examine and improve workplace operations, including staffing and workload, schedule control, administrative burden, safety, communication, and access to support. Individual self-care can complement but not replace system-level improvement.
source_row.source_detail: CDC/NIOSH Impact Wellbeing Guide — systems approach: address organizational drivers such as staffing, workload, schedule control, administrative burden, safety, leadership and access to support rather than relying only on individual resilience. Current NIOSH Impact Wellbeing guidance; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. source_row.stem: A nurse manager sees rising burnout, short staffing, unpredictable schedules, and excessive administrative burden. Which intervention best reflects NIOSH's systems approach to worker wellbeing?
